notes: The A.7 matrix prices six documentation deliverables individually with staggered due dates (8, 10, 12, 24 weeks) that run business-process documentation then design/API/data-model then migration plan, and payment is released only on CA acceptance, which is the gated chain; it is not milestone_payments_only only because the deliverable order is substantively sequential rather than just dated, and a reader who treats the sequence as inferred rather than stated would land on the alt.

A one-year Docebo SaaS subscription plus a one-time onboarding fee, with all three deliverables due on the same date six days after award and nothing being built; recurring_operations is the reasonable competing read since the vendor hosts and supports the platform for a year, so the split is licence-purchase versus ongoing service.

Only the DC Supply Schedule cover page extracted: a 365-day NTE $500,000 audit and financial management schedule whose supplies/services line reads 'Other (Delineated in each Task Order)' and whose prices are an unextracted Attachment A price list, so nothing in the readable text describes delivery; a reader willing to infer that a DCSS labor-rate vehicle is by nature a capacity buy would say incremental_capacity.

An IDIQ for key-box hardware priced per key space plus one annual software licence and hourly installation and maintenance labor, with the deliverables table being nothing but the hardware CLINs by location; it is not recurring_operations because the base year is overwhelmingly an equipment and licence buy and the option-year maintenance is a small hourly add-on.

Supplemental acquisition staffing billed by the hour against a $10M annual ceiling with personnel supplied 'on an as needed basis' to any District agency through task orders, so scope is set order by order and can be redirected freely; not recurring_operations because nothing is being operated or maintained, only staff supplied.

The base year carries a real dated waterfall chart (Kick-Off, Analysis/Requirements, Process Documentation, Design Review, Design Approval sign-off, Wireframe Development, Application Development, Customer UAT, UAT Acceptance/Go Live) with billing milestones and sign-off deliverables, so the gates are backed by dates and money; flagged because the four option years are pure licence, hosting and support, and a reader weighting the price schedule's annual subscription CLINs could call the whole thing recurring_operations or goods_or_licenses.

A sixteen-line F5 part-number order (BIG-IP appliances, transceivers, 12-month support subscriptions, prepaid consulting hours, training) delivered within 30 days of award with option years of licence and support renewal only; no work is described beyond shipping and prepaid hours, so no other label is in play.

A DC Supply Schedule MOBIS IDIQ that adopts a GSA hourly rate card, is described as the vehicle for agencies' recurring requirements, and whose only contract-level deliverables are a quarterly sales report and the catalog price list, so all real scope arrives later in task orders; structure_not_stated is the defensible alternative because the vehicle never says how any particular engagement will be delivered.

A fixed annual price ($248,313.60 per year) for Agilent Advantage Bronze repair coverage and standard preventive maintenance on named lab instruments, with a single deliverable line of 'on site' service across the year; not goods_or_licenses because no equipment or licence is being purchased, only service on instruments already owned.

Only page 1 of 31 extracted: a single $594,386 lot line reading 'Base Period - System Implementation, Licensing, Maintenance & Support' for Seon bus video systems, with pricing in an unextracted Attachment B, so there is no schedule, no deliverables and no described work to judge; goods_or_licenses is the reasonable alternative if the line item alone is taken as a product buy, and recurring_operations is a third live reading, which is why this one has no settled answer.

An open-ended human care agreement with no committed quantity, paying regulated per-service rates as roughly 1,000 vocational rehabilitation referrals arrive and continuing indefinitely with monthly progress reports; the honest competing read is milestone_payments_only, because each referral does pay against an approved per-person chain (intake/assessment report, employment plan, placement, stabilization) and a reader focused on that chain rather than on the vehicle would pick it.

Sole-source continuation of software support, hardware support, hosting and ticket paper for an existing e-citation system, priced as annual lump sums with response/resolution SLAs and a deliverables table whose every due date is literally 'On going'; not goods_or_licenses because the paper and printer coverage are incidental to the support subscription.

Stated scope is maintenance and support of an existing system and the four option years are nothing but technical support, hosting, warranty and consumables (~$53k each), which outweighs the base year; flagged because roughly $72k of the $117k base year is a one-time hardware expansion (three ALPR camera systems, tablets, mounts, installation), so a reader weighting the base year alone would reasonably say goods_or_licenses.

Five named advisory roles bought as blocks of hours (520 to 2,080 each) at burdened rates to oversee a separate vendor's UI benefits system build, with output being weekly and monthly status, requirements and assessment reports rather than a build chain; flagged because the document reprints the other vendor's Inception/Analysis and Design/Construction/Transition Gantt, which invites a false sequential_gated_deliverables read of work this contractor is not performing.

Six base-year deliverables are priced separately and chained on approval of the one before (work plan, then preliminary needs assessment 'within three months of the approval of the work plan', then final needs assessment 'within one month of DBH approval of the preliminary', then preliminary plan, final plan, implementation plan), so scope is fixed and each stage is a paid gate; flagged because nothing is built or tested, and a reader who reserves this label for design-then-build work would say milestone_payments_only.

A one-year firm-fixed-price buy of the Skillsoft LMS and its prepackaged courseware, with the contract's own definitions section built around "License User" and "Skillsoft Product(s)"; not recurring_operations because nothing is being operated or maintained for the District, only access licensed to it.

Labor-hour NTE ceiling against a fully loaded rate schedule, incrementally funded, with a scope of plan review and oversight that ends in "Other services related to DCCR and mega projects as requested" and an F.3 that has no deliverables table at all; not recurring_operations because the price is hours drawn down, not a recurring fee, though a reader who weighted the never-ending review workload over the pricing could land there.

An IDIQ bench with a $100 guaranteed minimum, no limit on task orders, and all real scope and dates pushed into future task orders, so work is directed as DMPED's priorities change without modifying the contract; the F.3 line here is the boilerplate sentence and carries nothing, and a reader could fairly say the award document simply never states how any piece of work is delivered.

Every CLIN in every year is a quarterly "On-going Operational Costs" line, and the surviving C.5 heading reads "Contractor Support and Maintenance Activities shall include:" over a category/resolution-timeframe table; the extracted text has lost most section bodies, but what survives is a maintenance retainer and nothing else.

Scope is frozen as an enumerated feature list and the SOW itself runs requirements-gathering to implementation to documentation to post-implementation support, which is a real chain rather than boilerplate; the weakness is that the three deliverables all carry the same 9/30/2021 due date and the price is a single $388,000 lot, so no gate actually controls payment.

Bug resolution, Tier 2 support, one-business-day outage response, monthly hour reports and named full-time staff priced as annual lots, with every option year relabeled "support and maintenance"; the base year does contain a genuine one-time BBL Online migration to the Microsoft business portal (requirements gathering, architecture, code migration), so this is a mixed build-plus-support award that a reader could reasonably split, and the dedicated-headcount framing also supports incremental_capacity.

Six specific, scope-defining deliverables run from current-state mapping through capability assessment, vision, strategic approach and an implementation roadmap, which is a substantive chain rather than the standard form; against that, the whole period of performance is three weeks, every deliverable carries the identical due date, and the price is one $581,400 lot, so nothing is actually gated.

Priced as identical per-year CLINs for licensing/hosting/user support, project management, user training and "Annual Configuration", with deliverables due "as needed over period of performance" or "by end of period of performance"; goods_or_licenses is the near miss because the license and hosting line is the largest single CLIN, but the contract caption and the bulk of the work are maintenance of a system already in place.

Four project-specific phases (Clean Up, Data Flow analysis and requirements, Implementation, Launch with UAT and production deploy), a deliverables table whose column heading is "Consulting Acceptance Criteria for Payment" with Week 4/8/12 dates running in sequence, and a written acceptance procedure; the counterweight is that Attachment B prices the whole thing as hourly labor categories with min/max hours and the implementation deliverables are "MVP Iteration 1/2/3", so the money does not actually pay per stage.

Draft plan 6/15/2026, final plan 7/1/2026, assessment framework 7/15/2026 and future state plan 9/30/2026 run in dated sequence, with a stated review-and-revision cycle and "Payment shall be contingent upon acceptance of deliverables by the CA"; nothing is built here, it is a consulting study, so a reader who reads sequential_gated_deliverables as requiring a design-then-build chain would call it milestone_payments_only.

An IDIQ with a $100 minimum, a $500,000 maximum, a fully burdened hourly rate card and a single named consultant sold as 500 hours of Power Platform advisory support; there is no deliverables schedule anywhere, and the SOW is phrased throughout as "support may include", which is a block of capacity rather than a defined operations service.

The CLINs are recurring activity categories priced identically in every option year, and F.3 sets their cadence as monthly reports, quarterly summits and trackers, bi-weekly calls and an annual report; milestone_payments_only is the near miss because each recurring activity is separately priced, but nothing runs in a one-way sequence.

UNRESOLVABLE UNDER THIS SCHEME: the base year splits almost exactly in half between a one-time build (Website Redesign Implementation $108,075 plus Content Migration $16,375) and annual operations (Hosting Maintenance and Support $96,035 plus E-Mail/M365 Administration $29,099), and the deliverables mix a UAT-for-approval gate and a migration plan with SLA uptime targets and incident priority tiers; I chose recurring_operations because all four option years drop the build entirely and are hosting and email administration only, but a rater weighting the base year alone would defensibly say sequential_gated_deliverables and neither reading is wrong.

Every line item is a Palo Alto part number tied to a named device serial number for a one-year subscription or premium support renewal, with no work described at all; recurring_operations is the near miss only because "premium support" is in the item names, but the support is the vendor's, sold as a SKU.

Annual CLINs for web hosting, LMI maintenance, Virtual One Stop maintenance, job spidering, TAA maintenance, document imaging and VOS Greeter, repeated unchanged across four option years, with 24x7 support and no deliverables table in Section F at all; goods_or_licenses is the near miss because VOS is the vendor's COTS product, but what is bought is its continuous operation.
